description: Small labeled IR collection for BM25 evaluation. Relevance grades: 0=irrelevant (omitted), 1=partially relevant, 2=highly relevant.

documents.d01: BM25 is a probabilistic ranking function used by search engines to estimate relevance of documents to a query.
documents.d02: Okapi BM25 scores documents using term frequency saturation and document length normalization with parameters k1 and b.
documents.d03: Inverted indexes map each term to the list of documents that contain it for fast boolean retrieval.
documents.d04: TF-IDF weights terms by how often they appear in a document and how rare they are across the collection.
documents.d05: Precision at k measures the fraction of the top k retrieved documents that are relevant to the query.
documents.d06: nDCG discounts graded relevance gains by rank position and normalizes against an ideal ranking.
documents.d07: Tokenization splits text into normalized word tokens after Unicode case folding and punctuation removal.
documents.d08: Python is a popular programming language for building information retrieval prototypes and machine learning pipelines.
documents.d09: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building HTTP APIs with automatic OpenAPI documentation.
documents.d10: Elasticsearch implements a variant of BM25 as its default textual similarity scoring model.
documents.d11: Average document length is a corpus statistic used by BM25 to normalize long and short documents fairly.
documents.d12: Document frequency counts how many documents contain a term and is the basis of inverse document frequency.
documents.d13: Boolean AND search returns only documents that contain every query term without ranking by importance.
documents.d14: Neural re-rankers use transformer embeddings to reorder an initial candidate list from a lexical retriever.
documents.d15: Stop words are very common terms that some retrieval systems discard before indexing or querying.
documents.d16: A query with only unknown vocabulary terms should not retrieve meaningful lexical matches.
documents.d17: Hand-calculated BM25 examples verify term frequency and IDF components against a trusted reference.
documents.d18: Evaluation datasets pair queries with graded relevance judgments so ranking quality can be measured.
documents.d19: Unix pipes connect command-line tools; they are unrelated to search ranking algorithms.
documents.d20: Gardening tips for watering tomatoes in summer heat have nothing to do with information retrieval.
